key_insight: Task-aware imputation can outperform standard reconstruction-focused methods when missing-data patterns differ between training and test time, because predictive utility and reconstruction quality are only weakly correlated.
engineering_relevance: For deployed ML systems with incomplete tabular data, imputation should be chosen and validated against downstream prediction performance under realistic missingness shifts, not just reconstruction error.
method: Unified task-conditioned optimization framework for treating missing entries as variables
Amortized imputation for missing data at both training and test time
Latent optimization approach for settings where only training data are incomplete
evidence_signal: The study evaluates 98 tabular datasets and tests robustness under train-test mismatch on 36 datasets, finding weak reconstruction-vs-prediction correlation (Spearman rho ≈ 0.16–0.32).
watch_item: Task-aware methods add optimization and modeling complexity, so gains may depend on how well the assumed missingness mismatch matches deployment conditions.
paper_title: When Does Task-Aware Imputation Matter? An Analysis of Robustness Under Train-Test Mismatch
